12 journal prompts for burnout

Most journal prompts assume you have energy to reflect. Burnout is the condition of not having that, which is why the usual gratitude questions land so badly when you are in it. These twelve are written for the flat weeks: short, concrete, and answerable in three lines when three lines is all you have.

Noticing where you actually are

  1. What did today cost you that yesterday did not?
  2. Name the last time you felt genuinely rested. Not asleep. Rested.
  3. Which part of your week are you already dreading, and when did it start being like that?
  4. If someone described your month back to you without using the word "busy", what word would they use?

Finding what is draining it

  1. What are you doing out of habit that nobody would notice if you stopped?
  2. Which task takes ten minutes and which one only feels like it does? Write both down and compare.
  3. Who gets your best attention right now, and who is getting what is left?
  4. What have you said yes to this month that you would say no to if asked today?

Finding what is left

  1. What is one thing that still works — small, unglamorous, reliable?
  2. When did you last do something badly and it was fine?
  3. What would the next two weeks look like if you were allowed to do the minimum?
  4. What is the first thing you would put down, if you were told you had to put one thing down?

How to use them without making it another task

Pick one. Not four. Set a timer for five minutes and stop when it goes, even mid-sentence, especially mid-sentence. Burnout gets worse when recovery turns into another thing you are failing at, so an unfinished answer is a finished session.

Is it burnout or is it something else

Burnout, ordinary stress, and a low mood all feel similar from the inside and want different things from you. Stress or Burnout: How to Tell the Difference is free to read and lays out where the line usually sits. If it has gone on for months, or if it has followed you into the parts of your life that are supposed to be the rest, that is worth taking to a therapist.

Common questions

Do journal prompts help with burnout?

They help you see where the drain is coming from, which is usually the hard part. They are not a substitute for changing the load or for professional support when burnout has gone on for months.

How long should I spend on one?

Five minutes on one prompt. Stopping mid-sentence is fine and often better than finishing.

Is the Theraglee journal private?

Yes. Journal entries stay in your own account. No therapist can see them, including when Theraglee Match Mode is switched on.

What is the difference between burnout and stress?

Stress is usually too much, and it eases when the load does. Burnout is what is left after too much went on too long, and rest alone often does not touch it.
